original_question: Is there a Riemannian metric on a closed manifold with everywhere positive sectional curvatures and ergodic geodesic flow?
target_in_paper: Question 8.1.1 in Section 8.1 ("Ergodic geodesic flows") of the final arXiv/ETDS version; in the accessible 2014 submitted PDF this same problem appears as Question 8.2.1 in Section 8.2 ("Positive curvature").
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's intended problem almost verbatim: it is an existential question, it is specifically about a Riemannian metric (not Finsler), the manifold is closed, the curvature assumption is everywhere positive sectional curvature, and the dynamical requirement is ergodicity of the geodesic flow.
missing_details: The quantifiers are implicit: the question asks whether there exist a closed manifold M and a Riemannian metric g on M with the stated properties.
Because sectional curvature is involved, the manifold is implicitly of dimension at least 2.
To make the question fully stand-alone, one should say that the geodesic flow is the flow on the unit tangent bundle SM of (M,g).

Question 8.1.1 itself does not restate the invariant measure, but elsewhere in the paper the authors formulate ergodicity questions with respect to the Liouville measure; that is the natural implicit interpretation here.
The nearby remark that metrics close to the round metric on S^2 would be especially interesting is motivation, not part of the formal statement.
refined_question: Does there exist a closed smooth manifold M of dimension at least 2 and a Riemannian metric g on M such that K_g(\sigma) > 0 for every 2-plane \sigma \subset T_xM at every x \in M, and such that the geodesic flow on the unit tangent bundle SM is ergodic (with respect to the Liouville measure)?
justification: The draft matches the official problem the paper isolates in its discussion of ergodic geodesic flows. In the final version, Section 8.1 first asks the broader question whether every closed manifold admits a Riemannian or Finsler metric with ergodic geodesic flow, and then narrows to the positive-curvature Riemannian case as Question 8.1.1. The wording of your draft is already essentially identical to that question. The only additions needed for a fully stand-alone formulation are to make the existential quantifiers explicit, note the implicit dimension restriction coming from sectional curvature, and spell out that the flow is the geodesic flow on SM. The paper does not explicitly add the measure in Question 8.1.1, but its ergodicity questions elsewhere are stated with respect to the Liouville measure, so that is the natural implicit meaning here. The remark about metrics close to the round S^2 is contextual motivation and should not replace the formal question.
